flashinfer: 0.7.3 stock pinned release; verify loaded wheel and native providers
hardware: one exclusive H100; same allocation for both arms
checks: eager vs graph logits original/changed/restored inputs
no new profiling in serving or warm process
skip-op, disable tuning, disable graphs, cache reuse off
strict miss and error restoration controls

performance.order: ABBA then BAAB; two independent cold seeds per arm, fresh warm serving processes
metrics: synchronized full decode path wall time
performance.criterion: For every tested shape, paired median scoped/baseline latency <=1.03; if excess or CI includes >1.03, investigate and repeat only the ambiguous case. No statistically supported regression accepted. Neutral within noise is sufficient. Separate cold startup from serving.

publication: source and results on leejnau fork; no PR until user requests
numerical_padding: 3->4 and 7->16 additionally check padding; performance matrix remains batches 1/4/16
shared_compilation_caches: Triton and CUDA driver compile caches shared from admitted pilot for both arms; FlashInfer autotune stores remain isolated per arm/seed. Cold means cold tactic cache; initial full-JIT pilot is recorded separately.
measurement_policy: Unspecified in both arms; preserve operation-owned timing settings.

design_refinement.reason: Forced graph policy produced a reproducible approximately 0.6% batch-16 slowdown against one baseline cache. Narrow this integration to scoped ownership/persistence and retain operation measurement settings. Preserve the complete original cohort separately.
design_refinement.new_cohort: Fresh tactic caches, same ABBA/BAAB ordering, geometry, source dependency and hardware. No pooling with prior forced-policy results.

startup_placement_refinement.reason: The measurement-unchanged cohort retained a reproducible approximately 1% batch-16 loss for one cache pair. Same-stream preparation did not fix it. A copied-cache matched-winner control was neutral, and preparing beside original warmup recovered the faster timings in a separate diagnostic.
startup_placement_refinement.scope: Managed decode cache prepared alongside existing startup warmup; no measurement-policy override. Reuse disabled retains the existing legacy path.
startup_placement_refinement.final_cohort: Independent fresh caches, ABBA/BAAB order, unchanged sizes/timing protocol; preserve both prior cohorts separately.
startup_placement_refinement.ready: Pending final-head controls, numerical comparisons and performance analysis; do not infer readiness from a diagnostic.

numerical_follow_up.trigger: A second scoped cold seed failed predeclared pointwise logit parity; fresh warm reuse reproduces it. One-entry change recovers parity.
numerical_follow_up.native_reference: On one real down-projection input, -1/0/1 pass against FP32; 1 has smaller maximum and relative-L2 error. This is not evidence of a native correctness defect.

accuracy_plan.arms: same preserved failed cache; legacy versus scoped; no retuning or new selections
accuracy_plan.purpose: Quantify model-answer impact of the implicated candidate, preserving the failed pointwise check. Report paired answer changes and total scores; not the repository CI benchmark or proof of general equivalence.

numerical_follow_up.readiness: Withheld; neither relaxed tolerance nor copied-cache recovery counts as natural-selection success.

final_preserved_winner_timing.reason: All native probes pass vs FP32 and fixed answer accuracy is 146/200 legacy vs 155/200 scoped. Measure the actual preserved choices without silently passing the failed pointwise-parity screen.
final_preserved_winner_timing.order: ABBA, four fresh warm processes on the same natural cold cache pair
final_preserved_winner_timing.cache: original failed scoped seed 1, unchanged v1 and managed files
final_preserved_winner_timing.numerics: Retain all error flags; still require finite output, exact top1, changed/restored-input checks and no profiling. Mark runs with failed allclose completed_with_numerical_differences, never passed.
final_preserved_winner_timing.timing: Same six shapes, 20x50 replay blocks and 5x64 decode steps; no new tuning or candidate search.
final_preserved_winner_timing.limits: One cache pair, two process observations per arm; descriptive timings only, no equivalence or serving-throughput claim.
